topics.title: useEffect Deep Dive
topics.description: Master the useEffect hook by visually understanding when it runs, how dependency arrays work, and the cleanup function.

overview.what: useEffect lets you perform side effects in function components. It replaces lifecycle methods like componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate, and componentWillUnmount.
overview.when: Runs after every render by default. You can control it using the dependency array.
overview.why: Helps you synchronize your React component with external systems (API calls, subscriptions, DOM manipulation, etc.)

keyConcepts.title: Empty Dependency Array []
keyConcepts.description: Effect runs only once after initial render (like componentDidMount)

keyConcepts.title: With Dependencies [count]
keyConcepts.description: Effect runs when any value in the array changes

diagram.description: Step-by-step flow of the useEffect lifecycle

steps.title: Component Renders
steps.description: React renders the component and commits it to the DOM

steps.title: Check Dependencies
steps.description: Compares current vs previous values using Object.is()

steps.title: Run Cleanup
steps.description: If previous effect exists, run its cleanup function

interactiveDemo.title: Try it Yourself
interactiveDemo.explanation: Click the button below to change 'count' and watch how the effect behaves.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to include all dependencies in the array (causing stale closures)
Causing infinite loops by updating state inside useEffect without proper dependencies
Not returning a cleanup function for subscriptions or timers
topics.proTip: Always run ESLint with the react-hooks/exhaustive-deps rule enabled. It will warn you about missing dependencies.

topics.title: useState & Automatic Batching
topics.description: Understand how useState works internally and why React 18+ automatically batches state updates for better performance.

overview.what: useState is the most fundamental hook that lets you add state to functional components.
overview.when: Use it whenever you need to store and update data that affects what is rendered.
overview.why: It triggers re-renders when state changes and React 18+ batches multiple updates to avoid unnecessary renders.

keyConcepts.title: State Initialization
keyConcepts.description: useState returns current state and a setter function

keyConcepts.title: Automatic Batching
keyConcepts.description: Multiple setState calls in one event are batched into one render

keyConcepts.title: Functional Updates
keyConcepts.description: Use callback form when new state depends on previous state

diagram.title: How useState & Batching Works
diagram.description: State update flow and automatic batching in React 18+

steps.title: State Update Called
steps.description: setCount() or similar setter is triggered

steps.title: Update Queued
steps.description: React queues the update instead of re-rendering immediately

steps.title: Single Re-render
steps.description: One final render with all batched updates applied

interactiveDemo.title: Try Batching Demo
interactiveDemo.explanation: Click the button to see how multiple state updates are batched into one re-render.

commonMistakes: Using the current state value directly instead of functional updater
Expecting immediate state update after setState
Not understanding that state updates are asynchronous
topics.proTip: Always use the functional form (setCount(prev => prev + 1)) when the new state depends on the previous one.

topics.title: useMemo & useCallback
topics.description: Learn when and why to use useMemo and useCallback to prevent unnecessary re-renders and expensive calculations.

overview.what: useMemo caches expensive calculations. useCallback caches function references.
overview.when: Use them when passing values or functions to child components that use React.memo.
overview.why: Prevents child components from re-rendering unnecessarily when parent re-renders.

keyConcepts.title: useMemo
keyConcepts.description: Memoizes the result of expensive computations

keyConcepts.title: useCallback
keyConcepts.description: Memoizes function definitions to keep stable references

keyConcepts.title: Dependency Arrays
keyConcepts.description: Both hooks rely on correct dependency arrays

diagram.title: How useMemo & useCallback Work
diagram.description: Caching mechanism to optimize React performance

steps.title: Parent Re-renders
steps.description: Parent component re-renders due to state change

steps.title: Return Cached Value
steps.description: If dependencies same → return cached result/function

steps.title: Child Stays Stable
steps.description: Child component does not re-render unnecessarily

interactiveDemo.title: Try Performance Optimization
interactiveDemo.explanation: See how useMemo and useCallback prevent unnecessary recalculations and re-renders.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to add dependencies to the array
Using them on simple values that don't need memoization
topics.proTip: Only use useMemo and useCallback when you have a measurable performance issue or when passing props to memoized child components.
